This activity will develop and validate a flexible, modular and future-proof eLORAN/GNSS signal simulator, synchronised with commercial GNSS simulators and supported by dedicated Receiver Analysis and Validation Tools. The simulator will provide high-fidelity signal generation, propagation modelling, multi-chain and multi-time-reference capabilities, and record-and-replay functions, enabling realistic end-to-end validation of resilient PNT solutions across timing, maritime and other application domains.

original.description: Objective: To define and assess the feasibility of a digitally controlled, highly efficient and compact High-Power Amplifiers in L-band / C-band for PNT applications.Description: With the increased demand for navigation services, the number of signal componentstransmitted by a GNSS satellite has increased. Since constant envelope multiplexing schemes are not suitable (or inefficient) with ahigh number of signal components, modern GNSS systems generate signals with high PAPR (Peak to average Power Ratio). DC power efficiency is critical for high power amplifiers (HPA) transmitting signals with high PAPR. In the last decades several HPA architectureshave been investigated to solve this limitation. Among those, the category of polar transmitters such as Envelope Tracking (ET) andEnvelope Elimination and Restoration (EER) stand out for high efficiency and excellent thermal management of the transistors. Conversely, they showed major challenges such as high complexity and difficult implementation with wideband signals. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. The challenge of analogue envelope reconstruction can be overcome by a digital modulator, leveraging recent advances in digital technologies. Atthe same time, evolution of PNT services is moving beyond L-band, targeting C-band or other frequency bands with larger bandwidths,where there is no example of dedicated HPAs for navigation. This activity will investigate amplifier design solutions to address high PAPR narrow band, as well as medium PAPR broadband signal configurations. The amplifiers will include digital predistortion, to achieve high-quality PNT signal performance, and compact designs to target advanced payload architectures. The selected designs willbe demonstrated through the development and testing of elegant breadboards (EBB) This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of the operational scenarios and end-to-end user requirements associated. - Literature review, oriented at the latest developments in ET and polar transmitters in general, in analogue and in digital domain, as well as in broadband HPA solutions - Trade-off and down-selection of the most promising technologies based on the survey and preliminary high-level studies - Breadboards detailed design, and analysis and preparation of manufacturing plan and test plan - Breadboards manufacturing and test - Critical analysis of the results obtained and future roadmap.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. original.description: The frontiers for the deployment of 5G cellular networks have grown beyond the limits of the Earth's atmosphere. The 3GPP cellular technologies have become attractive for exploration missions, such as Moon or Mars, as they can provide a standardised scalable, secure, high-capacity, and reliable connectivity. For Moon, the Space Frequency Coordination Group (SFCG) has recently identified several bands for Lunar missions for the deployment of existing Earth communication protocols that includes the cellular element. In parallel to the connectivity, 5G networks can also be used to enhance the performance of navigation services fores een in LunaNet.The communication services will be primarily delivered by satellite-based solutions (already identified in the LunaNet architecture for the Moon). However, although the lunar relay satellites could technically provide surface-to-surface communications for a small number of users, such approach does not scale well as the number of users increases.To serve larger number of users, wireless cellularnetworks on the lunar surface are foreseen. With such deployments, an opportunity to offer 5G space user terminals emerges on the market. A new space-grade 5G user terminal will thus need to be developed, leveraging the technologies from 5G ground terminals, and making them available for exploration missions. This activity will design, manufacture, and test an engineering model of a 5G user terminal in FR1 for exploration missions. To achieve this, the activity willleverage on the current standards, techniques, and technologies. The activity will:- Review and consolidate the connectivity use cases of 3GPP networks in exploration missions (Moon and/or Mars)- Identify potential future exploration missions- Define and study architecture and scenarios of 5G cellular networks that could provide connectivity and enhanced navigation.- Design and implement an engineering model of 5G user equipment, including a test equipment, for connectivity in exploration missions.- Test the connectivity and positioning performance of the 3GPP networks using the developed test equipment.- Develop a roadmap to reach a flight model with integration of LunaNet navigation receiver capabilities

original.description: Space Weather Centre for Spain Initial Establishment and Core Capability Developments: Part 1This activity will constitute the initial establishment and operation of a Space Weather Centre for affected stakeholders along with underpinning tools, capabilities and procedures required in order to deliver tailored high quality services to end users. Key user groups are expected to include operators of energy transmission systems, satellite operators, the aviation sector, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) and others. The Centre shall operate in close cooperation with ESA's Space weather Service Network with the aim to establish a node that facilitates collaborative actions with network participants while moving progressively towards a structure with a clear operational dimension ableto support the development and delivery of tailored space weather capabilities and services. Particularly the centre will focus on translating complex space weather information from multiple sources into streamlined, actionable information. A colocation of the development and operations teams shall be foreseen with the aim to streamline the R2O process, support team building and to encouragedirect feedback to research, optimising the use of facilities in ESAC.Part 1 shall include: Systematic mapping of end users and establishment of key contact points with users and stakeholders Establishment of a proactive engagement strategy and actions with the identified end users to ensure full understanding of end user needs and operational requirements Development of necessary IT infrastructure, tools and service operation procedures in order to operate the space weather front desk, initially on an 8/5 basis, with on-call support during periods of elevated space weather activity. OoProcedures shall be developed with a view to transitioning into full 24/7 support at the start of a future Part 2 of this activity. Operation of the space weather front desk from KO+3 months for at least 6 months prior to the start of Part 2 handover Development of a space weather dashboard capabilities targeting end users and building on well demonstrated and tested space weather assets, constituting a layer for translating complex technical concepts into an easy-to-use tool for end users. Training for end users including exercises and simulations based on realistic use casesDevelopment of a roadmap for the operational Centre including priority R2O needs and the inclusion of a space weather testbed facility to be used for regional event simulations and training, bringing together stakeholders including end users, operators and domain experts with a focus on optimising the R2O2R pipeline. Support for data and product provision from existing assetsas part of the service provision shall be foreseen where it does not duplicate activities already funded via the Space Safety Programme's pre operational space weather service activities. Operationalisation of certain key models and tools along with their re-deployment within the Centre may be foreseen subject to the necessary licensing agreements with the asset owner. A handover to Part 2of the activity shall be foreseen.

original.description: EL1-134 - This activity will investigate innovative techniques to enable continuous optical timing and ranging links under all weather conditions, addressing a key challenge for operational optical PNT (Positioning, Navigation, and Timing) systems. Optical satellite-to-ground links, such as those planned for ESA's OpSTAR mission, are vulnerable to atmospheric effects, particularly cloud cover, which can degrade or completely interrupt communications with an Optical Ground Station (OGS). The study will assess and experimentally demonstrate atmospheric transmission enhancement techniques designed to improve link availability under adverse weather conditions. It will evaluate whether these approaches can maintain accurate and reliable timing and ranging measurements between laser terminals representative of future operational optical PNT systems.

original.description: This activity investigates concepts for providing on-demand PNT services during crises by leveraging satellite communication systems. It aims to support continuity of positioning, navigation, and timing when terrestrial infrastructures fail due to natural disasters or humanitarian emergencies. The study will identify relevant use cases, define system concepts and requirements, and assess feasibility through preliminary designs. It will also demonstrate key components and functions via small-scale laboratory proof-of-concept setups. The outcome will include a mission study, roadmap, and verification report for future demonstrations. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity
